target_audience.primary_persona: Individual consumers seeking to build and maintain positive habits through gamification and visual tracking
secondary_personas: Productivity enthusiasts who want cross-platform habit tracking
Users who respond well to playful/gamified interfaces (cat theme)
People who need gentle accountability and motivational support
Users who prefer mobile-first experiences with web fallback
pain_points: Difficulty maintaining consistency with habit formation
Boring or overly complex habit tracking apps
Lack of motivation after missing days
Need for visual progress tracking and streaks
Forgetting to complete habits without reminders
Wanting to track habits across multiple devices
goals: Track daily progress visually with streaks and calendars
Stay motivated through gamification and positive reinforcement
Get timely reminders for habit completion
Review analytics to understand habit patterns
target_audience.usage_context: Daily use on mobile devices (iOS/Android) and web, primarily during morning routines, throughout the day for habit check-ins, and evening reviews. Users expect quick interactions with minimal friction.

product_vision.one_liner: A playful, cat-themed mobile habit tracker that makes building good habits fun through gamification, time-aware suggestions, and visual streak tracking
product_vision.problem_statement: People struggle to form and maintain habits because most tracking apps are either too complex, boring, or don't provide adequate motivation after setbacks. Users need a delightful, low-friction way to build consistency.
product_vision.value_proposition: Unlike traditional habit trackers, Daily Habits Tracker combines a charming cat-themed personality with smart features like time-based habit suggestions, visual streak chains, and gentle gamification to make habit building enjoyable rather than a chore.
success_metrics: Daily active users (DAU) and retention rates
Habit completion rate (habits checked vs habits tracked)
Time-based suggestion chip engagement (40-60% improvement claimed)

existing_features: Habit creation with emoji and color customization
Habit streak tracking and chain visualization
Week view and calendar views for habit history
Notes attached to individual habit completions
Analytics dashboard with heatmaps and visualizations
known_gaps: Habit reorder mutation not implemented (TODO in App.tsx)
Widget support for iOS/Android home screens
Advanced recurring habit patterns (e.g., every 3rd day)
technical_debt: TODO: Implement reorderHabits mutation in convex/habits.ts
Multiple API key integrations that need maintenance

differentiators: Time-aware habit suggestions adapt to daily rhythms
Cross-platform with web and mobile sync via Convex
Lightweight gamification without overwhelming RPG complexity
Modern tech stack (Expo 54, React 19, Convex realtime)
competitive_context.market_position: Positioned as a friendly, approachable habit tracker for users who want gamification without the complexity of Habitica, and personality without the austerity of minimalist trackers. Appeals to users who value delightful UX and cross-platform access.

technical: Dependency on Convex cloud backend for data persistence
Clerk authentication integration for user management
Expo managed workflow limits native module flexibility
Multiple LLM API keys suggest AI feature dependencies
resources: Small development team (primarily 1-2 contributors based on git history)
Mix of manual and automated development (Cursor Agent, Vibe Kanban in commits)
dependencies: Expo EAS for builds and deployment
App Store / Play Store for distribution
